explanation: This slide contains a diagram comparing prokaryotic and eukaryotic DNA replication. In prokaryotes, replication starts at a single origin of replication on the circular chromosome and moves bi-directionally. In eukaryotes, multiple replication bubbles form along the linear DNA molecule at multiple origins of replication, eventually merging to yield two complete daughter DNA molecules.

questions.q: In the diagram comparing replication types, what shape is the chromosome in prokaryotic replication?
questions.exp: Option B is correct because the diagram illustrates prokaryotic replication on a circular chromosome, which is a characteristic of prokaryotes mentioned on previous slides.
